message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $103 and am on B_O_RAILROAD. I own the pink and orange monopolies, plus WATER_WORKS and MARVIN_GARDENS. p2 has $564 but is weak. p3 has $147 and is in jail.

p3 has dark blues with one house each, brown hotels, and many mortgaged properties. p4 has $3101 but is in jail.

p4 is the runaway leader with $3101 and light blue hotels. I block p4's yellow monopoly by holding MARVIN_GARDENS, which they need for Atlantic and Ventnor. p4 also has Pennsylvania Avenue, completing their green monopoly.

p4 is in jail on turn two and may get out next turn. I cannot unmortgage NEW_YORK_AVENUE because my cash is too low.

I cannot build houses either. I will keep holding my blockers and avoid trading with p4.

I am weighing whether to trade with p3. Their dark blues with one house each are not a major threat yet, but adding houses would make them dangerous. I will not trade with p4, since that would feed the runaway leader.

p3 could bankrupt p4 and inherit Boardwalk and Park Place, which would be catastrophic. p2 has $564 but is weak. I need cash to survive light blue hotels costing $550–$600. I am calculating mortgage values for my pink properties.

My mortgageable equity totals $535, giving me $638 in combined cash and liquid assets. That covers one light blue hotel hit without pre-mortgaging. I will not mortgage now because of the 10% interest and lost rent income. My current unimproved rent is $10 per pink and $14 per orange.

With New York Avenue mortgaged, I cannot collect doubled rent on the orange monopoly. Water Works and Marvin Gardens rent are too low to justify pre-mortgaging. I will keep my properties unmortgaged and only mortgage when forced by debt.

I am now calculating whether building houses on the orange monopoly is viable. New York Avenue is mortgaged, so I cannot unmortgage it for $110 with only $103 cash. Even if I could, three houses would cost at least $300 and would not yet yield enough rent to threaten p4.

Three orange hotels would yield roughly $1500 in rent, but I lack the cash to build them. I cannot threaten p4 myself in the near term.

I am now considering trading with p3. They hold mortgaged reds and greens, plus dark blues with houses and brown hotels. They might want my orange pieces, though I already own the full set.

I cannot trade away my orange monopoly to p3 because they lack any orange properties. p4 only wants my yellow and pink pieces, which I will never sell. p2 has little value to offer, and selling North Carolina would not complete a green monopoly. I am now considering whether buying anything useful is worthwhile.

I considered selling Water Works to p2 for cash. That would only yield about $100–$150 and sacrifice a small rent source. It is too marginal to justify a trade proposal, and I can still take other post-turn actions before ending my turn.

I will not propose a trade. A rejected offer wastes a turn action and could reveal strategy. p4's strength comes from light blue hotels, cash, and railroads. No trade can break that position.

p4 is still collecting rent while in jail, so their hotels remain dangerous. I am on B&O Railroad and this is my turn's post-turn action decision.

I rolled a 5 from Free Parking to reach B&O Railroad. p3 owns that space but has mortgaged it, so I collect no rent.

I considered selling my pink properties to p2 to block p4's pink monopoly, but that would let p2 flip them back to p4 for a fortune. Selling Marvin to p2 carries the same risk. I will not trade away any blockers.

I will not trade away any property that could complete a monopoly for p4, and I will not give p2 anything they could flip back to p4. Selling Water Works to p2 would only yield about $50–$100, which is too little to matter. I am now considering whether proposing a trade directly to p4 could help without strengthening them.

I will not open negotiations with p4. I cannot bankrupt p3 or p2 with my tiny rent income, so the only way they could die is by landing on my properties. That would give p4 Park Place and Boardwalk, which would be catastrophic for me. The game is a grind where p4 slowly chips away at everyone else with light blue hotels.

I am now calculating whether p3 could survive a light blue hotel hit by liquidating their mortgaged properties and brown hotels. If they can, they might become a threat again. I will end my turn and hold position without making any risky moves.

Selling Water Works to p2 would only raise cash to about $203. That is still too little to unmortgage New York Avenue and build houses. I cannot afford the $410 needed to fully develop the orange monopoly. Trading away a single orange would break my own monopoly, so that is not an option.
